name: Gramme-type dynamo generation
description: Gramme-type electromagnetic machines generated electrical power and were demonstrated as reversible.

impact.note: Sold to industry and lighting works in several countries; steady machine-made current became practical, and electric lighting and power engineering grew from it.

places.note: Place refers to the sourced event; historic political boundaries are not inferred.

date.basis: Date stated in the cited source.

events.statement: The Musée des arts et métiers attributes improvements to existing electromagnetic generators to Gramme in 1871.

evidence.supports: Museum describes Gramme’s improvement of electromagnetic generators in 1871 and Fontaine’s demonstration of reversibility in 1873; the catalogued object dates circa 1880 and is not identified as the demonstrated machine.

events.caveats: A museum attribution, not a claim that all generators originated then.
